policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'his holy ones' is plural, matching the qere בִּקְדֹשָׁיו, but the ketiv בקדשו is the common defective spelling of the same 3ms plural suffix (-ו for -יו) and is read 'his holy ones' too; the English cannot tell the two orthographies apart. No textual note is mapped to this unit. Base fallback (qere) retained.

ASV 'he is waited for of the sword' renders a singular passive participle with the sword as agent, which is the qere וְצָפוּי 'he is watched for'. The ketiv וצפו is an active plural 'they watch/have watched', which would yield 'they watch him for the sword' rather than a passive with 'of the sword' as agent; the ASV's construction excludes it.

ASV 'in vanity' renders שָׁוְא/שָׁו in either spelling; the qere בַּשָּׁיו and ketiv בשו differ only orthographically and both mean 'in vanity/emptiness'. Nothing in the English wording, no italic supply, and no mapped textual note distinguishes them. Base fallback (qere) retained.
